manual_rationale: Lower true-microgravity chromatin-regulatory program at both MHU-2 sites
Lower under true microgravity at both MHU-2 sites but heterogeneous across missions
Lower true-microgravity epithelial and follicular signaling at both MHU-2 sites
Lower true-microgravity barrier-lipid program at both MHU-2 sites
Lower pooled and true-microgravity barrier and tissue-coordination program
Lower adaptive immune communication in 8 of 10 de-duplicated cohort sources
Lower adaptive immune signaling in 9 of 10 de-duplicated cohort sources
Lower T-cell receptor signaling is the strongest adaptive signal and matches prior reduced splenic T-cell abundance and activation after flight.

Lower splenic degranulation-program scores are consistent across all five unconfounded projects, seeds, ssGSEA, GSEA, and composition adjustment. This extends prior evidence of altered neutrophil regulation but is not a direct assay of neutrophil degranulation or suppressive function.
Lower C-type lectin sensing is consistent across all five projects and all five checks, extending the known immune dysfunction phenotype to pathogen-recognition circuitry.
Higher ECM proteoglycan activity agrees with renal matrix dysregulation and profibrotic structural adaptation reported across spaceflight kidney datasets.
Higher aggregate WNT program scores across all six projects extend prior gene-level reports of WNT dysregulation; they do not imply that every WNT ligand, including Wnt11, is higher.
Higher IGF transport connects growth-factor availability to the matrix-repair response; this is a pathway-level extension rather than a demonstrated increase in IGF protein activity.
